references.text: Moses refers to the same argument that the Egyptians would say the Lord brought the people out to kill them in the mountains, which threatens God's honor among the nations.
Moses repeats the concern that the people in the land they left would say the Lord was not able to bring them into the promised land.
The Lord fears that the enemies would misunderstand the situation and say their own hand was strong, not that it was the Lord who acted.
Joshua expresses similar concern about what the Canaanites would think of the Lord's name if Israel were wiped out.
Reference to the promise the Lord gave to the fathers to bring them into the land, which is also mentioned in our text.
God's oath to Abraham to bless his descendants, which is the basis for the promise of the land mentioned in the verse.
The context where Moses argues that Egyptians and other peoples will hear about Israel's fate and draw conclusions about the Lord's power.
